nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Which groups are mentioned as being more affected by eco-grief?
nodes.answer: Youth and individuals working or studying in environmental and land-based fields are identified as being more affected by eco-grief.
nodes.paragraph: People from different demographic groups may experience eco-grief in different ways. Experiences and emotional reactions are also often entangled with other lived realities, such as social inequities or large-scale disruptive/traumatic events (e.g., the recent global COVID- 19 pandemic) ([Citation removed for blind peer review]). The nascent research shows that some groups are more affected, including youth and people working and studying in environmental and land-based fields (L ger-Goodes et al., 2022 ; Clayton & Karazsia, 2020 ; Ojala, 2012 ; [Citation removed for blink peer review]). People who engage in land- based activities and (or) livelihoods are at exceptionally high risk because they witness acute and chronic environmental change as part of their interactions with land (Cunsolo & Ellis, 2018 ). 13 Human EcologyMethods Theoretical Framework Several studies have investigated lived experiences of climate change and its influence on people S emotions (Budziszewska & Jonsson, 2022 ; Jones & Davison, 2021 ; Kemkes & Akerman, 2019 ; Verlie, 2019 ). For this study, we use interpretative phenomenological analysis (IPA) to explore observers thoughts and feelings associated with the environmental forms of degradation that they are witnessing and learning about through their roles.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Fair access to green jobs_qna_001
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How can policymakers address the potential unemployment crisis in the fossil fuel-based energy generation sector during the transition to renewable energy sources?
nodes.answer: Policymakers can introduce skill-development facilities to help workers in the fossil fuel-based energy sector develop new skills and transition to employment opportunities in the renewable energy sector, thereby mitigating the unemployment crisis.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Fair access to green jobs_qna_002
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What percentage of the funds from the Next Generation EU programme is proposed to be allocated to the green transition in Spain?
nodes.answer: 39% of the funds that Spain receives under the Next Generation EU programme is proposed to be assigned to the green transition.
nodes.paragraph: Also, the NECP envisages the need for higher taxes on heavily polluting activities. The Technical Building Code laysdown new building regulations, to ensure that domestic energy consumption is low. A fundamental driving force behind many of these initiatives will be the Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan (RTRP), presented by the Spanish Government inOctober 2020, which proposes assigning 39% of the funds that Spain receives under the Next Generation EU (NGEU) programme to the green transition; see Cansino et al. (2016) for a description of the policy measures to control carbon emissions in Spain. Ensuring that energy policies are as effective as possible requires an understanding of the main dynamics and drivers of emissions. Within this context, the interest in modelling and forecasting GHG emissions is without doubt. Carbon dioxide (CO 2) emissions, largely by-products of energy consumption, account for the largest share of GHG and, consequently, the analysis of GHG emissions has usually focused on CO 2 emissions; see, for instance, Friedlingstein et al. ( 2022 ), who describes the Global Carbon Project that produces world-wide projections of CO 2emissions in preparing the annual Global Carbon Budget, which is considered in the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPPC) reports.
